title: A line longer than about 268 MB x columns makes Segment.thin loop forever and trap on step overflow.
detail: `while bytes / Int64(count) * Int64(step) < 4096 { step *= 2 }`. `bytes` is the nominal segment size (4 MB), but a segment owns every row of a line that starts in it. Once it holds more checkpoints than bytes, bytes/count == 0, the loop never ends and `step *= 2` traps on overflow. Trigger: one line longer than about 268 MB x columns, wrap on (default). 10 GB line crashes below about 37 columns (narrow quick-view pane, zoomed font; columnsThatFit goes down to 20). 50 GB line crashes below about 186 columns, which includes the default window. Reproduced with the real 4 MB segment size: a 300 MB line at textWidth = 1 gives Trace/BPT trap (m6).
fix: Thin by the span the segment's rows actually cover (first checkpoint offset to end of last row), in floating point or as count * 4096 / span, and clamp step. Better: cap checkpoints while scanning by doubling the stride once a segment exceeds N checkpoints.

title: stopWork() on the main thread synchronously closes idle pooled readers, so a stalled SFTP/FTP server freezes the UI.
detail: stopWork() runs on the main thread and calls loaded?.source.close(), which closes every idle pooled reader synchronously. SFTPFileReader.close() does channel.request(.close, timeout:), default 30 s. FTPReader.close() does abortTransfer(), which waits up to 10 s for a reply. Idle readers are exactly the ones not cancelled, so they take the synchronous path. Trigger: quick view or Lister on an SFTP/FTP file; server stalls; press Down, F2, N/P or close the window. UI freezes for the timeout, once per idle reader. On a healthy server it is still a main-thread round trip per file change.
fix: Hand close() to a background queue (ProviderByteSource.close/deinit, CachedByteSource.close); also mark the readers interrupted first so they take the closeHandleLater path.

title: HTML page mode allows meta-refresh navigation (type .other), so a hostile HTML file loads a remote page.
detail: Every navigation of type .other is allowed. A <meta http-equiv="refresh"> is delivered as .other and the CSP meta tag does not restrict navigation. Trigger: HTML file with meta refresh to http://host/..., shown in page mode (mode 4). The web view requests the URL and renders the remote page with its own subresources and no CSP: tracking, IP leak, GET requests against localhost or intranet devices. Reproduced in m5: local server received GET /refresh then GET /img.png. JavaScript stayed off, file:// targets were blocked, and every other vector tried (img, css, iframe, object, video, font, @import, ping, form) was blocked.
fix: Allow only the first navigation (about:blank or the WKNavigation returned by loadHTMLString) and cancel all later ones. Optionally add a WKContentRuleList that blocks all network loads.

title: ProviderByteSource.open measures symlinks/special files by reading the whole file with an uncancellable loop, hanging on /dev/zero or FIFOs.
detail: Three parts. (1) LocalFileSystem.item(at:) reports size = 0 for anything whose lstat type is not a regular file, including a symlink to a regular file; the viewer then measures by reading the whole file before showing a byte. (2) The measuring loop never checks the cancel flag; it relies on reader.interrupt(), a no-op for the local reader, so moving on does not stop it. (3) item.isSpecial is ignored. Triggers: F3 on current.log -> big-50GB.log gives minutes of "Reading..." and every F2 or cursor move leaves another thread reading 50 GB to the end. A symlink to /dev/zero (trivial to ship in an archive) or /dev/zero itself: a thread spins forever, even after the window closes. A FIFO: open() blocks forever, one GCD thread per visit; enough of them exhaust the pool.
fix: try cancellation.throwIfCancelled() inside the loop; refuse or specially handle isSpecial; use the resolved size for symlinks (stat); open local files with O_NONBLOCK and fstat for S_ISREG.

title: Giant lines get sparse checkpoints (and quadratic partial publishing), making page fetches and row(containing:) slow once indexing completes.
detail: Same root cause as finding 1 for giant lines that do not crash. Sparse checkpoints: thinning assumes a 4 MB span, so checkpoints end up 4096 x (line bytes / 4 MB) apart, up to twice that from integer division. Measured: a 256 MB line gives 820 checkpoints, 327 KB apart (m2); a 4 MB line in the scaled test kept one checkpoint. Extrapolated: 10 GB line -> 10-20 MB decoded per page fetch or row(containing:); 50 GB -> 50-100 MB; over a server past the 1 GB spill cap, that is downloaded per scroll step. Fast while the index is partial (stride 64), slow the moment indexing completes. Quadratic partial publishing: each partial publish retains the checkpoint arrays, so the next append copies the whole list every 4 MB; about 30 GB of memcpy for a 10 GB line at 80 columns, hundreds of GB for 50 GB (computed).
fix: As in finding 1, plus publish partials without sharing the growing array (append-only chunks).

title: CharacterBoundaries indexes past a short read, trapping when a cp932/936/949/950 file shrinks while searched.
detail: data[data.startIndex + $0] is indexed up to the requested length, but a source returns short data once the file has shrunk. Trigger: a cp932/936/949/950 file is truncated or rotated while open, then the user searches with a text or regex pattern. Reproduced with a shrinking source: trap (m3 crash).
fix: Bound by data.count; treat a short read as end of file.

title: TemporaryCopies.localURL uses a percent-decoded lastPathComponent, allowing path traversal and truncation of an arbitrary user-writable file.
detail: Temp file name is url.lastPathComponent, which percent-decodes. sftp://h/dir/..%2F..%2Fx yields "../../x", and folder.appendingPathComponent then escapes the per-copy folder and the temp root (m9). createFile(atPath:) truncates whatever exists there. Trigger: any non-file URL with %2F in its last component reaching a mode needing a local copy (media, Quick Look), e.g. a link in an HTML page or a URL handed to ViewerService.view. An attacker-controlled server could overwrite a user-writable file with its own content. Not affected: names from directory listings, which isSafeName filters.
basis: traversal mechanics reproduced (m9); end-to-end reachability plausible
fix: Sanitise to a single component (replace /, :, NUL; reject . and ..), or always use a fixed name plus the extension; verify the standardised target stays under folder; create with O_EXCL.

title: RTF NSTextView and PDFView have no link delegate, so clicking a link in an untrusted file opens any URL scheme.
detail: Clicking a link in an untrusted RTF or PDF goes to NSWorkspace.open with any scheme: file:///.../x.command, smb://attacker/... (mount and credential leak), or app URL schemes. Related: followLink (ViewerPane.swift:627-630) loads any non-http URL from a page through the provider registry, which may be a network provider with an attacker-named host.
basis: inferred (plausible; framework default behaviour, not run)
fix: textView(_:clickedOnLink:at:) and pdfViewWillClick(onLink:with:) that pass only http/https/mailto, or strip .link attributes. Restrict followLink to the base file's own file system and folder tree.

title: HTML page mode and RTF accept files up to the 1 GB wholeFileLimit and process them on the main thread.
detail: HTML: decoded to UTF-16 (2 GB) and a String, then policy + html is concatenated and loadHTMLString is called on the main thread. RTF: parsed in background, then setAttributedString and layout run on the main thread. Trigger: press 4 on a 900 MB .html log, or open a large RTF (RTF opens rich by default).
fix: Cap both at tens of MB, as htmlTextLimit does, and fall back to text.

title: One serial fetchQueue per pager blocks all later fetches (including the next file) behind an uninterruptible read; stuck builds/loads pile up on GCD.
detail: One serial queue per pager serves all documents. A read the kernel will not interrupt blocks every later fetch, including those of the next file. The local reader has no interrupt(), so this applies to stalled SMB/NFS/AFP mounts and dying disks. Also: each show starts an index build on a global queue and each load starts a workQueue job; stuck ones pile up towards GCD's thread limit and can stall other global-queue work.
fix: A queue (or operation) per document so a new document never waits behind an old one; cap in-flight builds and loads; for local files use non-blocking or F_NOCACHE reads with a watchdog, or at least stop issuing new reads on a source with a stuck one.

title: ScaledFrameCache starts uncancelled, unchecked resample jobs for every draw size, burning cores and 1-2 GB on zoom.
detail: Every distinct draw size starts a job on the global queue. Jobs are never cancelled and do not check the generation before working. Each allocates up to 160 MB and resamples the full frame at high quality. Trigger: Ctrl+wheel or pinch on an 8192^2 image: dozens of stale jobs, about one per core at a time; on the order of 1-2 GB transient plus all cores busy, and the wanted bitmap arrives last. Related: while no bitmap is ready, draw resamples the full frame with .high on the main thread (:173, :187).
fix: One serial queue; check a LatestNumber before scaling; debounce about 100 ms; use .low/.medium for the interim draw.

title: Save As truncates the target before reading, so choosing the viewed file as the target destroys it.
detail: Save As calls createFile(atPath:contents:nil) on the target before reading. If the user picks the file being viewed (the panel offers its name and confirms "Replace"), the file is truncated to zero and then "copied" from itself (data loss).
fix: Refuse a target that is the same file (fstat dev/inode), or write to a temporary file and rename.

title: Backward case-insensitive search returns the match at the start position itself (Straße / strasse), so Find Previous repeats the same hit.
detail: The search range is extended by length - 1 units past end. A case-insensitive match shorter than the needle (ß for ss, Straße for strasse) can begin exactly at end; a backward search then returns the match at start itself. Trigger: Find previous for "strasse" in a text with "Straße": after the first hit every Shift+F3 returns the same hit. The search fuzz (7,706 runs) found only this mismatch (m3).
fix: Reject found.location >= end and continue before it.

title: Any multi-frame image (.icns, .ico, multi-page TIFF, HEIC collections) is played as a 10 fps animation.
detail: Any source with count > 1 is treated as an animation with a 0.1 s default delay. .icns (10 representations measured), .ico, multi-page TIFF and HEIC collections become a 10 fps slideshow of different-sized images stretched into the first frame's rectangle. Report severity label: MEDIUM-LOW (correctness).
fix: Animate only when the GIF/APNG/WebP/HEICS dictionary carries delay or loop information; otherwise show the largest or first image.

title: Remote media/Quick Look files are copied whole to temp with no size limit or free-space check; two idle copies are kept.
detail: Cursor resting on a 50 GB .mov on a server puts 50 GB on the boot volume. Two idle copies are kept until the plugin stops. Report severity label: MEDIUM-LOW (performance).
fix: Size cap or free-space check; count idle copies by bytes.

title: FolderSummary lists with the non-cancellable provider.list and starts an unbounded recursive remote listing whenever quick view rests on a folder.
detail: Uses provider.list(_:showHidden:) although a variant taking cancellation exists. A listing on a stalled server cannot be interrupted and holds Parallel pool threads. Quick view also starts an unbounded recursive listing of a remote tree whenever the cursor rests on a folder. Report severity label: MEDIUM-LOW (freeze-adjacent).
fix: Pass the flag; for non-local volumes limit depth or entries, or require a key press.

title: HTMLText.plainText: a lone '<' swallows text up to the next '>' and href is matched by substring.
detail:
Measured in m9: `if a < b then ...

tail` yields "if a tail": a lone < swallows everything up to the next >. With no later >, the rest of the document is dropped (guard close < count else { return }). href is found by substring: `` shows and collects the decoy; `` breaks the tag.
fix: Treat < as a tag only before a letter, /, ! or ?; honour quotes when finding >; require a word boundary before href.

title: In HTML text mode the encoding menu changes codePage but the text is never re-decoded; read errors become an empty view silently.
detail: In HTML text mode the Encoding menu and A/S keys change codePage, but the stripped text is never re-decoded; the menu shows a new checkmark and the text does not change. `(try? read) ?? Data()` turns a read error into an empty view with no message.

title: block() keeps short blocks in the LRU, pread failure leaks budget, spill file lacks O_CLOEXEC, and long-scan path is not used with 256 KB blocks.
detail: block() keeps a short or empty block in the memory LRU (readAndKeep guards against this, block does not); after a transient short read later reads end early until eviction or F2. When pread fails the present bit is cleared but neither `held` nor the global budget is given back. The spill file is opened without O_CLOEXEC; a child spawned without close-on-exec defaults inherits a descriptor to cached remote content. With 256 KB blocks a 1 MB scan chunk is not "long" (> blockSize * 4 is false), so index scans of remote files go block by block through the LRU, contrary to the class comment; harmless for correctness.

title: Multi-byte code pages outside 932/936/949/950 (51932 EUC-JP, 54936 GB18030) are accepted by Other... but decoded single-byte.
detail: Multi-byte code pages that CF knows (51932 EUC-JP and 54936 GB18030 available here) are accepted by "Other..." but decoded as single-byte, so every high byte becomes U+FFFD. encode() for search still uses the real encoding.
fix: Reject them, or decode them through CF.

title: Re-layout triggers restart identical pending builds, zoom is not debounced, two full builds compete, and sequential scans read a giant line twice.
detail: pagerResized, applySettings and changeFontSize compare layout with the shown document, not the pending one, so a second trigger cancels and restarts an identical pending build. Zoom steps are not debounced: each starts a full index build (cancelled by the next). The shown document keeps indexing on all cores until the new one is adopted, so two full builds compete. A sequential (remote) scan reads a giant line twice: the owning segment reads to its end, then every following segment re-reads its own 4 MB while skipping.

title: TextRowIndex.segmentsReused is written under the lock and read without it (data race, test-only).
detail: segmentsReused is written under the lock and read without it (TextDocument.segmentsReused). Test-only but a data race.

title: Copy puts up to 64 MB text / 192 MB hex through pasteboard.setString on the main thread.
detail: Short main-thread stall: up to 64 MB of text or 192 MB of hex goes through pasteboard.setString on the main thread.

title: Print puts 2 MB into an NSTextView plus sizeToFit on the main thread.
detail: Short main-thread stall: 2 MB into an NSTextView plus sizeToFit on the main thread.

title: CodeTable.table(for:) can run on the main thread; a first DBCS table is about 24,000 CF conversions under a global lock.
detail: Short main-thread stall: CodeTable.table(for:) can run on the main thread. A first DBCS table is about 24,000 CF conversions under a global lock.

title: Row typesetting builds a CTLine per row (up to 2 x unwrapWidth = 32,768 units), rebuilt for all visible rows after every fetch.
detail: Short main-thread stall: CTLine per row with up to 2 x unwrapWidth (32,768) units, rebuilt for all visible rows after every fetch.

title: Index progress reaches the main thread unthrottled; each tick runs updateChrome, updateScrollers and possibly reveal/restoreCaret.
detail: Short main-thread stalls: index progress reaches the main thread unthrottled; each tick runs updateChrome, updateScrollers and possibly reveal/restoreCaret.

title: Row index for 50 GB of ordinary text or newlines is about 120-150 MB, doubled during relayout.
detail: One 12-byte checkpoint per 4-5 KB; about 120-150 MB for 50 GB, doubled while a relayout holds the old segments.

title: CharacterBoundaries.known grows without bound (one entry per 16 KB).
detail: CharacterBoundaries.known grows without bound, one entry per 16 KB.

title: No pixel-count check before CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex; a decompression-bomb PNG may be decoded in full.
detail: No pixel-count check before CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex; a decompression-bomb PNG may be decoded in full by ImageIO (plausible).

title: QLPreviewView is never stored or close()d, so its window never closes in the embedded quick view.
detail: QLPreviewView is never stored or close()d (ViewerPane.swift:597, dropRichViews). In the embedded quick view its window never closes. Plausible leak.

title: afterLoad closures of an overtaken fetch run after a later, unrelated load.
detail: afterLoad closures of an overtaken fetch run after a later, unrelated load.

title: topOffset falls back to the start of the file when the top row is not loaded, so a relayout during a fetch jumps to the top.
detail: topOffset falls back to the start of the file when the top row is not loaded yet, so a relayout during a fetch jumps to the top.

title: TemporaryCopies: a late localURL can insert a copy after release(owner:), and removeAll() during a copy leaves an entry whose file is gone.
detail: A late localURL can insert a copy after release(owner:) ran, so it is never idle. removeAll() during a copy leaves an entry whose file is gone.

title: Columns ignore East Asian width and combining marks; rows can split a base character from its mark or a ZWJ sequence.
detail: Columns ignore East Asian width and combining marks. Rows can split a base character from its mark, or a ZWJ sequence.

title: For RTL runs the selection rectangle uses to - from (negative), drawing a 2 px sliver.
detail: For RTL runs the selection rectangle uses `to - from`, which is negative, so it draws a 2 px sliver.

title: After a failed segment, rows walked from the previous segment overlap the numbering of the next.
detail: After a failed segment, rows walked from the previous segment overlap the numbering of the next.

title: A lookahead or match longer than 64 KB at a chunk border is cut (documented).
detail: A lookahead or match longer than 64 KB at a chunk border is cut (documented).

title: TextRowIndex and related shared state are sufficiently protected by locks or main-thread confinement.
detail: Table: TextRowIndex via NSLock (nesting new -> old only); scan state thread-local per segment; TextDocument.boundaries/fetchFailure own locks; CharacterBoundaries.known lock with `computing` serialising (order computing -> lock; waiters cannot be cancelled); CodeTable.tables static lock (apart from stall in finding 23); ProviderByteSource.idle NSLock, one reader per thread, cancelled reader closed never pooled, cancel/check-in race walked and invariant holds; DiskBlockCache instance state lock incl. pread/pwrite/close; DiskBlockCache.held budget lock (apart from leak in finding 19); CachedByteSource.blocks/order lock (double fetch harmless); TemporaryCopies lock with file I/O outside (apart from late-insert race, finding 25); LatestNumber/progressScheduled locks; ViewerPane, TextPagerView, ScaledFrameCache, ImageCanvasView, ListerSettings main-thread only, results gated by loadGeneration, presentGeneration, generation, revealGeneration and document identity; CancellationFlag handlers run outside the lock, reader interrupt() implementations short.

title: TextRowIndex.segmentsReused is the one shared-state item with insufficient protection (written under lock, read without).
detail: Listed as 'No' in the shared-state table; see finding 22.

title: Index equivalence fuzz: 6,000 cases found 0 mismatches against a single-pass decode reference.
detail: Raw scan (parallel and sequential, segments 16-1,024 bytes, chunks 16-4,096) compared with single-pass decode, including segment reuse into a second layout. Coverage: UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, 1252, 932/936/949/950; CR, LF, CRLF; tabs; NULs; junk bytes; columns 1-80; random access; row(containing:). Covers CRLF and multi-byte characters across borders, exact-width lines, bulk empty-line path, partial segments and reuse conditions.

title: Pathological 256 MB inputs are all linear and under 1 s.
detail: `\n` only: 0.03 s, checkpoints 4 KB apart. CR only, UTF-16 newlines, all tabs, all spaces, UTF-16 full of U+0A0A: all linear and under 1 s.

title: Unsafe buffer accesses in TextRows, ViewerSearch and HTMLText are guarded.
detail: Every unchecked buffer access traced is guarded. 16-bit handling is byte-wise or loadUnaligned. No pointer escapes its closure. Int32 offsets only relative to pieces of a few MB or less; file offsets Int64 throughout with the flag packed in bit 0.

title: Decoders map lone surrogates, overlong forms and values above U+10FFFF to U+FFFD; no zero-width unbounded row; no code page maps a high byte to TAB/LF/CR.
CharacterBoundaries invariant holds for the decoder as implemented.
detail: A non-lead byte is either a single-byte character or a trail byte, and both end a character. Half-width katakana are non-lead in the table.

title: Search: raw and decoded paths agree apart from finding 13; catastrophic regexes stop within about 50 ms of cancel.
detail: Includes i-dot, Kelvin, long s, ligatures, whole-word neighbours, chunk borders and backward search. Cancel of catastrophic regexes within about 50 ms (m8).

title: Spill file is safe: per-user temp dir, O_EXCL, mode 0600, unlinked immediately, never reopened by path; stops caching at the cap with no refetch loop.
Launch sweep deletes only when kill(pid, 0) gives ESRCH, so it cannot remove a live instance's folder; PID reuse only delays cleanup.
WKWebView setup is tight: JavaScript off, non-persistent store, baseURL nil; all subresource vectors blocked; only the meta refresh gets through.

Other checks sound: context-menu links limited to http/https/www; HTMLText linear on unterminated tags, comments, entities and skipped elements; no retain cycles; scroller and percent arithmetic safe, NaN harmless.
No run of the app, the test suite, or a build of the project; UI timing claims are from reading.
Behaviour of QLPreviewView, PDFKit, AVKit and ImageIO on hostile files not tested (remote loads in Quick Look SVG/Office/HTML previews, PDF page-count or rendering freezes, PNG bombs).
Whether network and archive providers accept %2F or foreign-host URLs end to end (finding 7) not checked.
Cost of seek in archive member readers not measured; archives report isLocal == true so they get the parallel index and random access.
ParallelPool and the kernel and providers beyond the reader close/interrupt paths cited were not reviewed.
Format.kilobytes traps for any value above Int64.max - 512, reachable from a ZIP64 entry or SFTP server size.
detail: Format.kilobytes computes (value + 512) / 1024. Trigger: a ZIP64 entry declaring an uncompressed size of 0xFFFF...FF, or an SFTP server reporting such a size. OpenArchive.swift:287 and SFTPChannel.swift:52 clamp it to Int64.max; two entries of 2^62 also saturate the total to Int64.max. The status line then calls Format.kilobytes(totals.totalBytes) at PanelViewController.swift:512. Trap reproduced (exit 133, t7 format); model returns Int64.max for two 2^62 items; chain verified link by link, not run end to end in the app. Also affected: DirectoryList.swift:117, SpaceCalculator.swift:116/121.

title: Format.speed and Format.duration convert a Double to an integer and trap on non-finite or huge values.
detail: e.g. remaining time for a near-Int64.max bytesTotal at under 1 B/s. Related to finding 1, low, plausible.

title: One stalled Parallel job takes every pool thread including the 4x reserve, leaving every Parallel.map serial.
detail: Workers always take open.first, the oldest job. If its pieces block (a size walk on a mount that stopped answering), every thread the watcher adds takes another piece of the same job and blocks too. Evidence (t8): a 64-piece compute Parallel.map took 0.08 s on a healthy pool; with one stalled 5000-piece job it took 0.65-0.84 s, close to serial, with 64 threads all blocked, as long as the stall lasts. Consequence: every Parallel.map in the app runs on its caller alone, including main-thread ones (PanelModel.areSameEntries, any Sorter.sort fallback on main). Deadlock: none, a caller only waits for pieces already in flight.
fix: Let extra threads (and preferably all workers) skip jobs whose in-flight pieces are all waiting, or take the newest job or round-robin. Cap the pieces of one job that may be blocked at once. Retire extra threads once runnable workers exceed width.

title: Extra pool threads retire only after 2 s idle, leaving 43 runnable threads on 16 cores after a stall ends.
detail: After the stall ended, 43 threads were runnable on 16 cores (t6 blocked) and stay so under continuous load.
fix: Retire extra threads once runnable workers exceed width.

title: run() counts idle workers that an earlier run() already signalled, so a second job can be left without help and without the watcher armed.
detail: Second job can be left without help and without the watcher armed (line 121).

title: While a blocked job has pieces left, the watcher re-arms every 20 ms indefinitely.
totalSizeByListing recurses once per directory level with no depth limit or cycle guard; a deep ZIP or endless server tree crashes the app.
detail: Evidence (t6 deep): a release build survives 4000 levels and dies with a bus error at 8000. The walk ran on a default 512 KB Thread, the same stack the pool's threads get. Reach: archive and remote file systems use this default (only local and virtual override). A ZIP with ~8k nested one-character folders crashes the app when Space is pressed on the folder (PanelViewController.swift:955). A server that returns a subfolder forever does the same, and never terminates before that.
fix: An explicit work list instead of recursion, or a depth limit of a few hundred levels (returning what was counted), plus a larger stackSize for pool threads.

title: The name comparison (localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare then compare) is not a total order: not antisymmetric in any locale, not transitive in da/nb/cy/es-traditional/hu/hr.
detail: Tests t2, t3, t4. Not antisymmetric in any locale: compare("й","ийтф") and its reverse both return descending; about 10% of random и/й pairs and 2% of е/ё pairs; some ligature pairs (fi, ß, dz). Not transitive in Danish, Norwegian, Welsh, traditional Spanish, Hungarian, Croatian for plain ASCII (e.g. 'aBa' < 'AA' < 'aAB' but not 'aBa' < 'aAB'). The ASCII gate is unsound: it passes for da, nb, cy and es@collation=traditional because 1- and 2-character names agree, but longer mixed-case digraph names do not; Sorter.sort then returns lists with adjacent inversions against areInOrder (97 in 200 small lists for da; '1aA' before '1AA'). No counterexample in en, de, cs, sv, fi, pl, tr, ja, zh and others. Adjacent checking cannot restore a total order that does not exist: with и/й or е/ё present the check fails whichever way the pair lies, so every such sort pays the single-threaded exact re-sort and every streamed batch pays an exact re-merge. Cost at 1M Cyrillic names (t5): sort 0.56 s -> 1.15 s; streamed load 2.3 s -> 6.1 s with worst single add 1.17 s; Hungarian ASCII names 0.55 s -> 2.0 s. Stability: result depends on the path taken (key sort, fallback, merge, reverse), so adding one non-ASCII file can reorder unrelated names. Memory safety holds with an inconsistent comparator.
fix: Make ICU the definition: compare by secondary-strength sort key, then by bytes. A true total order, needs no gate or check, and is already computed.

title: Background results are invalidated by changes that change nothing, and the fallback is full work on the main thread.
detail: update(with:) bumps listVersion even when it returns false (via setListed -> listChanged). setComputedSizes and applyFilter bump it too though listedItems is unchanged. On a stale version setFilter(_:prefiltered:listVersion:) filters the whole list synchronously; ViewOptionsPlugin.swift:200 falls back to model.setSort(order) on main. Scenario: 1M-entry folder with a steady stream of file-system events or arriving Space sizes; each header click or quick-filter keystroke then runs on the main thread. Measured on main at 1M (16 cores): setSort 0.16 s for ASCII names; a direction flip of non-ASCII names 0.6 s because resort calls NSString.compare per adjacent pair (line 125). setSort(_:presorted:) only checks the count, so stale content of equal length is accepted silently if a caller skips the version check.
fix: Bump the version only when listedItems really changed. On a stale version return false without doing the work so the caller restarts in the background.

title: PanelModel.Snapshot holds items but not filter or sort, so a failed open leaves a filtered subset with no filter shown, and restore can reinstate a stale order.
detail: Filter: shell snapshots, drops the quick filter, then calls open (PanelViewController.swift:601-603). If the read fails, restore leaves filter == nil with items still the filtered subset; panel shows part of the folder with no filter indicated, totals count the subset; a later setComputedSize silently swaps in the whole list (line 719). Sort: if the order changed while the folder was opening, restore brings back the old order under the new sort; the next direction flip reverses a list not in the assumed order: asking for ascending gave c, b, a.
fix: Put filter and sort in the snapshot, or re-derive items from listedItems on restore.

title: Whole-list PanelModel operations at 1M entries cost 0.07-0.35 s on the main thread, and setComputedSizes with a filter active is linear per name.
detail: Measured at 1M entries (t7 model), time on main: selectAll 0.22 s; invertSelection 0.35 s; totals after select-all 0.26 s; update(with:) with nothing changed 0.07 s per refresh; setComputedSizes (200 names, filter active) 0.15 s. With a filter active each name in setComputedSizes walks listedItems linearly (line 715): about 0.75 ms per name, so 10k sizes take about 7 s. The name index is rebuilt on main after every list change once three lookups happen.
fix: Index listedItems too when filtered, build the key sets off-main or incrementally, and count all-selected totals from the list totals.

title: Format uses one static NumberFormatter from pool threads and the main thread at once (not thread-safe); cached DateFormatter ignores locale/time-zone change.
detail: ContentColumn.value runs on background threads, several at once (Size on Disk column at PropertyDetails.swift:37), as do DirectoryList and NameList. NumberFormatter is on Apple's not-thread-safe list. No race detector run. Also: the cached DateFormatter never follows a locale or time-zone change. Report severity label LOW-MEDIUM.

title: FileMask matches by bytes: NFC mask misses NFD names, ? matches one byte, [ and backslash are fnmatch syntax, STRASSE* misses straße.

TextRowIndex.Segment.thin(spanning:) overflows and traps when a segment holds more checkpoints than bytes.
detail: `while bytes / Int64(count) * Int64(step) < Int64(TextRowIndex.minimumCheckpointDistance) { step *= 2 }`. A segment owns every row of the lines that begin in it. When it holds more checkpoints (one per 64 rows) than it is bytes long, bytes / count == 0, the loop never ends and step *= 2 overflows Int. Concrete: columns 1, segmentSize 1, one 66-byte line gives 2 checkpoints for a 1-byte segment. In the app with the 4 MiB segment it needs a single line of more than 268,435,456 rows: roughly a 27 GB file without line ends at 100 columns, or 2.7 GB in a 10-column window with wrap on. Reproducer repro/viewer/rows-thin-overflow.bin (75 bytes); confirmed on the unpatched release binary (SIGTRAP, arithmetic overflow at line 225). The copy was patched with a step < 1 << 40 guard (results/PATCHES.txt) so fuzzing could continue. Critical by the rule (viewing a file) but only for an extreme file.
fix: Use max(1, bytes / Int64(count)), or derive the step directly from count * minimumCheckpointDistance / max(1, bytes).

detail: The .text case of search uses range first ..< end + length - 1, assuming a match is as long as the needle. Without case, "ss" matches the single unit ß, so a match beginning exactly at end (the excluded start) fits and is returned. User effect: TextPagerView.swift:508 starts a backwards search at selection.lowerBound, so Find Previous would return the same hit every time (UI not run to confirm). Variant: with the start inside a character the returned match begins after the start (repro/viewer/search-backwards-returns-match-after-start-midcharacter.bin). Reproducer: FZ_STRICT=1 fuzz-viewer run search repro/viewer/search-backwards-returns-match-at-start.bin (23 bytes); without FZ_STRICT the driver tolerates this known case. Wrong result, no crash.
fix: After range(of:), reject any hit with found.location >= end and keep searching before it; do not size the range by the needle's length.

title: Search result depends on path and chunk size when ignorable characters are involved (case-insensitive NSString range(of:) ignores control characters).
detail: text.range(of: needle, options: [.literal, .caseInsensitive]). Once the text is not plain ASCII, Foundation's case-insensitive search ignores control and other ignorable characters (U+0000-0008, U+001B, U+200B etc.; not tab) on both sides (checked with a standalone NSString test). The raw byte path compares exactly, so the answer depends on which path a chunk takes. Such matches differ in length from the needle, so the range.length >= length and end + length - 1 arithmetic makes the answer depend on chunk size. Counterexamples: pattern "\u{1B}9" in bytes 39 AE (UTF-8): raw path nil, decoded path 0..<1 (repro search-raw-vs-decoded-ignorable-characters.bin, 11 bytes). Pattern "0\u{03}" in 72 bytes: chunked nil, whole 59..<60 (repro search-chunked-vs-whole-ignorable-characters.bin, 81 bytes). Inconsistent result, no crash. Both mismatch signatures share this cause (3 signatures, 2 root causes).
fix: Verify each NSString hit against the needle (folded units and length), or do the case-folded unit comparison yourself.

detail: append(_:) took 498-589 ms: all hits of one folder arrive as a single batch because walk (:280) only flushes in onDirectory. finish(items:groups:) took 448-543 ms: rebuilds rows from resultItems, counts directories and frees old rows, all on the main thread.

title: No Find result appears until a whole folder is done (first hit after 5.2-5.7 s name search, 42-53 s text search in a 1M-file folder).
detail: In the 1M-file folder the first hit came after 5.2-5.7 s for a name search (13 s for "everything") and 42-53 s for a text search; the window showed only "[Searching...]". Walk.deliver waits for node.pending == 0, meaning the folder is fully listed and every candidate tested.
fix: Deliver the already-tested prefix of a folder's candidates while the rest are pending, and stream the listing in batches.

title: One 202 ms main-thread stall waiting on the text-row index lock (TextPagerView.isIndexing -> TextRowIndex.isComplete).
detail: Happened once, on the single-line file, with about 65 threads contending in the storm; not seen on other files or without the hammer. Inferred: lock-holder preemption. Reported as low/medium.
fix: os_unfair_lock or atomics for the counters the main thread reads.

title: A file truncated during indexing is reported as complete with no error but fewer rows.
detail: Document ended with isIndexComplete == true, indexedThrough == length and readError == nil but fewer rows (e.g. 3.09 M instead of 13.35 M); rows(from:) then returned empty for known rows 704,854 times without an error. Removal of the file is reported correctly through readError. No crash or hang in any of the 12 rounds. Short reads are treated as end of text.
fix: Record an error when a read inside 0..<length comes back short.

title: Find cancel-to-finished reaches about 0.55 s (p95 489 ms) when a search of the 1M folder is cancelled, in the engine itself.
detail: Inferred: freeing the million-item candidate list.

title: A pager stopped with stopReading() reports isIndexing == true forever (document cancelled, never completed).
detail: Looks like the design, but anything waiting for indexing to end must handle it; the first smoke run waited on this indefinitely.

title: FindFiles correctness: every uncancelled search complete and duplicate-free, two runs same order, 8 concurrent tree searches all complete.
detail: Cancelled searches listed only a duplicate-free subset of the truth; searches after the torture still complete. Driven via FileSearch.run and the real FindFilesWindowController headless against independent readdir plus byte scan truth. Data: 100,002 files in 2,000 folders (903 MB) and a 1,000,000-file flat directory plus 200 folders.

title: Find timings: tree name *.txt 80,000 results 0.33 s; tree text 1,129 results 3.0-3.2 s; million name *7.png 16,667 results 5.2-5.7 s; million text xxxx 99,750 results 42.7-53.4 s; million everything 1,000,200 results 13.0-13.3 s.
detail: Stalls >8 ms in window phase: 3, 9, 1, 118, 5 respectively; max stalls 451 ms (harness), 32, 10, 59, 589 ms. 100 window-cancelled searches: 751 s, 457/9/2 stalls, product max 543 ms (2140 ms harness). 100 engine cancels from another thread: 588 s, 61/0/0, max 23 ms.

title: Find cancellation worked: 88 window cancels ended median 20 ms, p95 489 ms, max 549 ms; 12 finished before cancel; engine run returned median 12.5 ms, p95 492 ms, max 558 ms; none hung.
Find threads returned to baseline: baseline 19, 8-29 right after each round, 9 within 0.5 s of the last search.
Find memory: no growth in a tree-only run.
detail: Peak RSS 11.6 GB for the whole run including harness data. Malloc in use about 690 MB while search threads lived and 143 MB 5 s later, flat over 20 further text searches. Shorter million run ended at 1.1 GB in use (harness truth sets plus the window's kept result sets). CPU: 1,415 s user and 6,439 s system; million text search 209-389 CPU-seconds for 43-53 s wall.

title: Find stall attribution: product frames appear in only six stalls of 448-589 ms plus two AppKit layout passes of 120 and 248 ms with every core busy; the two stalls over 1 s and several others are the harness's own result checking.
Viewer indexing and first rows fast on all test files: first rows 11-24 ms; index 0.61 s (4 GiB dense), 0.85 s (sparse), 3.37 s (2 GiB single line, 7.5 CPU-s, not parallel), 0.15 s (1 GiB newlines).
Viewer row fetches after indexing: mean 0.15-0.26 ms, max 5.6-27 ms (single line mean 3.2 ms, max 8 ms); round-trip checks passed on all four files.
Viewer storm: 40 relayouts during indexing with readers, searchers and Esc ended with the last layout indexed and same rows/lines as the first; search returned at most 3.7 ms after cancel.
detail: 6 threads called rows/row(containing:)/row(ofLine:) with random cancels, 2 ran ViewerSearch.find.

title: Viewer truncate/remove during indexing: 12 rounds on 1 GiB all ended within 1.5 s with no crash or hang.
detail: Stalls 16/12/0 (all 12 harness), max 309 ms (harness), threads 9->42->11, peak RSS 26.5 GB. Removal reported correctly through readError.

title: FindFiles+Viewer: no crash, hang, deadlock, wrong result or thread leak at full scale.
Relayout reuse could not be shown on the dense file: the generator put one over-long line in every MiB so every segment needed rescanning.
heap and leaks on the live process hung, so the leaking object's type is inferred from in-process malloc statistics and the parallelism: 1 control.
Remote, spill-to-disk and double-byte code-page viewer paths not exercised (local UTF-8 only).
Spotlight and duplicate search modes not run.
Each scenario run once at full scale.
Find/viewer tables were headless and never drawn, so on-screen cost would be higher.
Machine load not quiet (26->13 for find, 11-24 for viewer, partly from the harness itself); a first find run overlapped another under the old lock and was discarded.
Searching inside a large file in the viewer drives memory to 44-97 GB.
detail: Footprint after 30 cancelled searches of the 4 GiB file went 7.9 -> 85.5 GB. On a 64 MB file each search added 60.8 MB at default parallelism against 1.0 MB with parallelism: 1; freed 5 s after the pool threads exited. Inferred cause: autoreleased NSData from FileHandle.read(upToCount:) accumulating in long-lived AFM.Parallel workers. Sources/ contains no autoreleasepool. (Relayed from the viewer fork, same as report 24 finding 1.)
fix: Wrap each piece in autoreleasepool in ParallelPool.perform (Parallel.swift:195), and likewise in FileSearch.swift:484 and TextRows.swift:331.

title: A dead share can stop every folder from loading: PanelLoader.stream calls volume(of:) without a cancellation flag, leaving one blocked thread per refresh.
detail: 82 blocked threads were enough that a local 300-file folder in the other panel did not open within 20 s (reproduced in both runs; main thread stayed responsive, max 30 ms). LocalFileSystem.volume(of:) uses resourceValues and statfs; a real dead mount was not tested so reproduction there is inferred. After leaving the share 8 calls stayed blocked (7 in volume(of:), 1 in places()) until the provider was released.
fix: Run provider questions on a bounded queue per provider (or one in-flight volume(of:) per location), give volume(of:) a cancellation flag, and never queue a second read behind one that has not answered.

title: A busy watched folder saturates the main thread: at 5,000 changes/s the panel applies 227-246 list updates in 20 s, each about 80 ms of main CPU.
detail: Main thread spent 18.1-18.3 of 20 s inside stalls. Same for a 2,000-file folder, so the cost is per update not per item. rereadIfDirty starts the next read as soon as one ends, and every update calls tableView.reloadData(). Scenario 8: 225/27/0 and 244/19/0 stalls, max 278 ms and 222 ms.
fix: Enforce a minimum interval between quiet reloads, growing with the cost of the last one; update only changed rows.

title: Every list change and cursor jump costs 9-110 ms on the main thread in the Full view (cells created rather than reused in the headless setup).
detail: FileListColumn.makeCell() still appeared in stall stacks seconds into a run. Whether an on-screen window reuses cells needs checking in Instruments.
fix: Draw rows directly, as the grid view does, or use frame-based cells without Auto Layout.

title: Marking in a huge folder blocks the main thread 0.3-1.3 s (select all 351 ms, invert 281-404 ms, select group by mask 333,336 hits 1,266 ms).
detail: PanelModel.selectAll / invertSelection and Selections.apply work on the whole list synchronously.
fix: Compute the new mark set in the background above the same 20,000-item threshold used for sort and filter, then swap it in.

title: An enabled-closure builds the whole operand list: Print enabled check costs 158 ms with 333k marked, paid whenever the Files menu validates.
detail: SystemToolsPlugin calls model().operands().filter... Asking all 332 commands costs 136-178 ms, of which cm_PrintFile is 158 ms and cm_ShowOnlySelected 19 ms; validating the Files menu costs 129 ms.
fix: Use hasOperandFile or a cached count.

title: Releasing a million-item list on the main thread costs about 0.5 s (leaving the folder, every quiet reload, shutdown).
detail: Leaving the folder 515-574 ms stall; 200 quiet reloads collapsed into 18-19 list updates in 90 s each stalling 500-670 ms inside PanelModel.update(with:) releasing the old array; shutdown shows 503 ms.
fix: Hand the old arrays to a background queue to release; consider not storing a URL per item.

title: Find window with about a million hits stalls 448-589 ms and no hit appears until a folder is fully done.
detail: append(_:) takes a whole folder's hits in one batch; finish rebuilds the rows on the main thread. First hit after 5.2-5.7 s for a name search and 42-53 s for a text search in the 1M directory.
fix: Flush by count as well as time, and deliver the tested prefix of a folder.

title: Utility-QoS work does not run for a minute or more when the cores are saturated (archive flush timer, column-value work).
detail: Evidence is the archive flush and column-value tests; QoS starvation as cause is inferred. Alternative for the archive tests is the min(60, 20 x lastRewriteDuration) idle delay at OpenArchive.swift:727.
fix: Raise the flush timer's QoS after a deadline.

title: watch is called on the main thread (PanelCoordinator.updateWatchers -> DirectoryWatcher.resolve -> realpath), which would block the window on a silent network mount.
detail: Not tested on a real mount. Also seen: watch called twice and capabilities(for:) 379 times from ButtonBarView.validate through a FileOperations enabled-closure on the main thread while the provider was silent.
fix: Set up watching off the main thread.

title: Parallel.map on the main thread deadlocks (and crashes with signal 5 if every body does it) if a body hops to main via DispatchQueue.main.sync.
detail: PanelModel.areSameEntries does call Parallel.map on the main thread, with pure bodies. The doc comment on Parallel.map does not forbid the hop. Sample saved.
fix: Document the rule and assert it in debug builds.

title: One-off SIGPIPE death (signal 13) of the PluginTests process, writer unknown.
detail: Once in the fourth full TSan run about 1,100 tests in; six re-runs with an injected SIGPIPE backtrace trap did not recur. The product sets F_SETNOSIGPIPE on its two pipe writers and uses NWConnection for sockets.
fix: signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) at program start as a safety net.

title: Viewer index lock: one 202 ms main-thread wait on the viewer's index lock.
detail: Relayed from fork.

title: A file truncated during indexing ends complete with fewer rows and no error.
detail: Relayed from fork.

title: About 1.4 KB of memory per ZIP member (272 MB for 200k).
detail: Relayed from fork.

detail: No shell code was found calling it on main. Relayed from fork.

An ASan + UBSan full-suite run had 1 timing assertion failure.
Every TSan full-suite run (4) had failures; none was a race report.

title: Scenario 1 (1,000,200-entry directory) timings: first rows 0.13 s (5,000 rows), complete 4.2 s, worst load stall 98 ms.
detail: Sort (name, ext, size, time, reversed) 0.30-0.32 s each with one stall of 103-110 ms; quick filter 0.13-0.25 s per key with a 77-109 ms stall; cursor model call 0.1-0.3 ms. Coming back: remembered rows after 0.15 s, fresh listing 4.3 s, five stalls of about 117 ms. detail: FileJob: no file lost, no partial file, no .afm-*.tmp, progress monotonic, cancelled jobs ended within milliseconds; deferred writes 581 good/32 failed commits with no source removed without commit. Archives: 804,155 and 742,286 reads matched; archive passed unzip -tq, zipinfo and the app's reader after each of 56 commits; cancelled reads median 0.1 ms (max 120 ms). FindFiles cancels median 20 ms, max 549 ms. Viewer index 0.15-3.4 s, no crash in 12 truncate/remove rounds.

leaks and heap hung on live processes, so the leak type in finding 1 is inferred.
